params.prompt: Five-second cinematic optical satellite observation film, 16:9, silent. Use the reference image for its realistic coastal remote-sensing appearance: open ocean on the left, land and estuary on the right, and a broad diagonal acquisition swath crossing the sea. Do not lock the shot to the exact still composition. Maintain a stable near-nadir satellite perspective while the observed coastline drifts smoothly through frame as the imaging pass progresses. The leading edge of the acquisition swath advances diagonally across the water, progressively revealing a restrained ocean-colour analysis treatment within its footprint. The revealed colour patterns remain geographically registered to the real estuary plume, coastal water and underlying sea texture. Keep terrain, shoreline and water geometry stable and photographic. The swath is a flat remote-sensing acquisition footprint, never a volumetric spotlight or glowing beam. No fictitious interface panels, text, labels, grids, warped coastline, dramatic zoom, low-altitude flight, or detached analysis graphics.

params.prompt: Create one continuous five-second photoreal corporate marine geophysics film. Use the supplied image as the vessel, temperate coastline, muted navy daylight and SINGLE grayscale seismic-section reference. This is an explanatory data visualization, not a physical wall. Wide oblique aerial camera; the whole modest survey vessel stays visible. The bow points LEFT, stern and wake RIGHT, throughout. 0-1s: vessel actively advances left along a straight survey line with a growing foamy wake and natural moving waves. Only a short translucent grayscale vertical data strip is initially visible below the track behind the stern. 1-4s: camera trucks smoothly left slightly slower than the vessel, creating visible vessel movement and real parallax against the distant coast. As the vessel advances, adjacent narrow grayscale seismic traces progressively append at the LEFT leading edge of the one flat section; acquired traces behind it remain spatially stable. A strong gently undulating seabed reflector with faint lower shallow reflectors becomes clearer as each adjacent trace is acquired. 4-5s: retain steady vessel movement, wake and camera tracking; finish showing the vessel plus a longer coherent acquired 2D section beneath its past track. The distant land geometry and vessel construction stay unchanged. Restrained elegant scientific visualization fully generated within this video. No cuts, no crossfade, no static photograph zoom, no physical solid curtain, no laser beam, no neon, no 3D geological volume, no extra planes, no text, no numbers, no logos. Keep the scene physically plausible, cinematic and readable silently.

params.prompt: One continuous photoreal five-second aerial coastal photogrammetry shot beginning exactly from this reference frame. The ONE six-rotor survey drone is a real modest-sized unmanned aircraft close to the camera, with the broad temperate coastline far below. It actively flies along the beach toward the distant upper-center bay, traveling diagonally away from its initial right foreground position. In the first second the six rotors spin rapidly and the drone gently pitches into forward flight. Through seconds 1-5 it travels steadily several body lengths away, gradually becoming smaller, with the underslung survey camera stabilized downward toward the beach. Preserve the same six arms, landing legs, body and camera throughout. The filming camera advances smoothly forward on a parallel path at a slower speed; nearby dune vegetation and sand move downward out of frame while distant headlands change slowly, producing strong natural spatial parallax. Small waves roll onto the shore and white foam advances and retreats naturally. Wide landscape scale remains dominant and the drone remains fully inside frame. Smooth confident cinematic motion and realistic daylight, natural blue sea, sharp terrain texture. No cuts or dissolves, no fixed-image zoom, no hovering in place, no sudden yaw, no extra aircraft, no changing coastline, no laser, no floating grid, no labels or graphics. This is actual-looking survey flight, not a diagram or an abstract animation.
